Fav: I really can't pick, see notes
Notes: Best songs: In the Flesh; Another Brick in the Wall, Pt. 2; Young Lust; Hey You; Comfortably Numb; The Trial. This album is lowkey masterpiece. The transitions between songs are fantastic and I feel like I'm going through a manic-depression period inside a dream. This was a hard listen because I'm not into rap and its hard for me to understand the lyrics. Perhaps a second listen through with subtitles will help. Also, Rap Snitches Knishes is good (and it was sampled from Space Oddity - Dave Matthews which is in the og Dune movie! - i found this out the day i'm gonna watch dune 2, crazy...)

Like the violin end in The Stars are Projectors. I think some track chunks are good, riffs are pretty solid. Best songs: Dark Center Of The Universe; Tiny Cities Made Of Ashes; The Cold Part; The Stars Are Projectors; I Came As A Rat. Honorable mentions for some chunks: Perfect Disguise; Lives. Also, I find it fascinating they capitalize every letter of each title. I haven't paid too much attention to the lyrics, but I think that's what makes them so good.

This is a fantastic album, but my listening experience was spoiled since I've heard so many of these songs before. The best include Exit Music (For A Film); Let Down; Karma Police; No Surprises. But overall, top tier album. This is one of the albums you must pay full attention to in order to experience all the crescendos with maximal instrumentation.

This album creates the sense of relief I feel when running, like I'm losing my burdens one by one. The buildup and instrumentation is on par with Radiohead's OK Computer, but I love the orchestral additions to it. Every song in this album is great barring Haiti (which I should probably give another shot). But otherwise, great listen.

The songs in this album are a little on the longer end and take a lot of twists and turns. It's not like I don't like it, but it's just not fully my vibe. Some sections are interesting but the interludes are a little dull. But some good songs include Dogs; Pigs (Three Different Ones), Sheep
Kinda mid.
It just felt like they wrote like 3 songs and duplicated them a bunch of times. not unique :(. EDIT: I went to their concert!

Fav: A Time To Be So Small
Notes: It wasn't super catchy, and the songs seemed relatively repetitive. Maybe it's just because I've been spoiled by the other music I listen to.
I've heard a lot of these songs before, so it wasn't too much of a surprise to me. They're like relatively good songs, but nothing spectacular.

I've only heard Atomized before, but since this was a Strokes side project, I had to check it out. Holy shit, it slaps.  Kubes; Atomized; Deep Red; Act of Contrition; O Please; City Walls; are song that are fantastic. They're all so different. It seems like Strokes but ethereal.

I'd only heard 'The Suburbs' track before, and had to continue with the Arcade Fire bs. This album has some emo-ish bangers. Top songs include: The Suburbs; Ready to Start; Empty Room; Deep Blue. My favourite thing about Arcade Fire is their use of orchestral instruments like violins for te buildups at the end. Their music, I think as mentioned in my review of 'Funeral' is the embodiment of release I feel when running.

Fav: High and Dry; Street Spirit (Fade Out)
Notes: Fav songs: High and Dry; (Nice Dream); My Iron Lung; Bullet Proof...I Wish I Was; Street Spirit (Fade Out). I think this album has a lot of potential; however, I listened to it not in the depressive Radiohead mental space I usually listen to their songs in. I've also heard a few of them before, so no surprise there. EDIT: Re-listening in a more Radiohead-suitable state of mind. Ok this is better than I thought. If I need to wallow or cry I wanna come here.

I've listened to the majority of songs in this album during my teenage years so nothing was majorly new. Since this album isn't super flowy, I can't say that the whole is greater than the individual here. However, most songs are definitely bangers. The only ones not as great are Semi-Automatic; Fake You Out; Guns for Hands; Truce. Even if this album doesn't rank super high in my reviews, I have an attachment to it because of my middle school days, so I owe it something (idk what, but definitely something).

I heard quite a few clips from this album before because Eilish is just that famous atm. I would say that most of these songs are good. Like I like listening to them; however, they don't particularly stand out to me. Eilish's voice is REALLY pretty but idk if this makes me sound musically spoilt, but its kinda old news at this point. But this album, and a lot of her other songs, make me appreciate FINNEAS's producer capabilities. He does the bulk of that stuff and is damn good at it too. But, I would say that it's kinda getting a little old and repetitive. He should prolly try and explore a few more things ig. I re-heard this and I think i love it now

I think I need to do anoter listen-through while paying attention to the lyrics and worlds created by TØP. They have been building something big ever since their previous album Trench. But the musicality of this album just ain't that great. They have some decent songs but idt any I'd listen to on their own. This is a bit sad since this band was my peak teen angst but we all grow ig, I am 20 now.
This is barely an album because it's 4 songs and 11 minutes long. It's very generic emoish rock music, so it doesn't particularly stand out to me in any way; it's filler music.

This is very typical daft punk music imo. There's some bangers in there and other songs are kinda mid. Like other songs by them, a lot of songs are very repetitive and make you wait a little too much for the good part (idk if this is my brainrot talking or is actually true). Top songs include Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger; Crescendolls; Superheroes; Something About Us; Voyager; Veridis Quo.

Fav: Why'd You Only Call Me When You're High?
Notes: I've heard many of these songs before because this is the Arctic Monkeys after all. Most are pretty good. I honestly don't even know what to say about it. I like all but Mad Sounds.
I'm relistening to this with the lyrics before writing my true thoughts.

I like this album; however, I don't know that it stands out to me. I'm not a huge fan of the first few songs (except Crying Lightning), but it ends pretty strong. I'm deciding whether this album deserves to go on my wall. Top songs include Crying Lightning; Cornerstone; Dance Little Liar; Pretty Visitors; The Jeweller's Hands.

Album: Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not
LeastFav: Perhaps Vampires Is A Bit Strong But...
Notes: I was quite surprised by how much I liked this album. It's the closest thing to punk rock I think I like. You have to be in a motivated? excited? some lowkey anger? type of mood for this to truly work.

I listened to the first half while running and that was a great idea! The first 8 tracks in this album are a slay and give me the electronic escapism vibes I love daft punk for. The songs like Beyond and Motherboard don't really do much for me as they sound a bit repetitive, but overall the album is a pretty good one!

Daddy Samburg is all I have to say. This man is the goofiest, funniest shit on the planet and this album embodies that. I didn't get some of the references made because this is from like 2007, but most songs were goddamn hilarious. I have yet to listen to this in a non-lyrical setting because the genius of this is in the lyrics not instrumentation and instrumentation is usually what I focused on. I'd like to think I'm growing as a listener (even if it's comedic lyrics)

Owen Pallett really makes everything better doesn't he? After listening to so many albums, it's super refreshing to hear one that makes me feel something. It's likely to do with the orchestration buildup that Owen Pallett does brilliantly like in Arcade Fire and the Her soundtrack. From googling, I think I like the Alex Turner heavy tracks as opposed to the Miles Kane ones. Also, the last track (The Dream Synopsis EP Version) is ;)))))))))–that sax...no words. Top tier. Reddit also says the lyrics are great, but I haven't listened to it yet.

I was a bit disappointed by this. I've heard a couple songs from this album before, but the rest were nowhere near that quality. They just felt like filler beats. Best songs include Let It Happen; The Less I Know The Better. I don't know why but I just expected better from this cause of all the hype it gets. I guess this kind of modern-electronic (non-Daft Punk) vibe isn't for me. But I do think I would like it a lot on shrooms.

This gives vinyl energy. The buildup in these songs is great. They're a lot slower than I'm used to, but this is probably stoner music ngl. For the full effect, you need to commit yourself to the album. It's not designed as background music.

LeastFav: Frances Farmer Will Have Her Revenge On Seattle
Notes: There's a lot of screaming going on. It's like grunge with metal-screaming. Best songs include Heart-Shaped Box; Rape Me; Dumb; Pennyroyal Tea; Tourette's. I just feel like there's not much going on in there; Kurt's just doing this thing and yelling again and again. I think listening to this again after 'Nevermind' would help me get acquainted to Nirvana's vibe.

I like this. It caters to my teen angst (who cares im 20) and angry grunge. Pretty much every song (except the last) is sexy. wtf is Territorial Pissings cause i love the song but what even is that name. Yummy

This wasn't really special in any way. I just like the vibe of most songs. Best songs include Rehab; Back To Black; and the song that has "What kind of fuckery is this?" Idk why I was disappointed because I don't have a strong opinion on most songs, it's just filler, intro-to-jazz vibes.

Idk why but this just didn't hit as expected. It seemed a little childish and quick, not like sophisticated. I really hoped for more, but 505 was the truest listen-again song. But I hoped for better because I like the Arctic Monkeys :(

Peak queen. This album feels like an intro into a raging musical/play obsession. I'm not sure why this doesn't hit at hard as it should tho. But I do def vibe with the last song cause it's like rock-invasion

Now I think we are getting back into the groove of things. This album finally has some good songs and the rest are all mid. But at least I can say that some are good. The album as a whole is pretty okay, but I give it props for the few good songs it has.

The only reason this album isn't an instant 'Buy!' is because idk if it'll sound good on vinyl. But, this album slapppppps. Discovered this in middle school and have listened to all these songs before (albeit out of order). Its just my kind of punk!
I didn't like this album that much. Some songs were okay, but maybe it's because I wasn't in the Radiohead headspace.

I listened to this while on a long slow run and I think it fits that vibe. This album is a little anti-dopamine-addict because each song is long and takes a little while to build up, but I still quite like it!

I've heard basically all these songs before, so nothing new there. But pretty much every song in this album is a banger. Idk how i feel about supporting jesse rutherford because of all the pedo allegations but the music is still good. It's very good in-between (chilling time but hype but not exciting me to run or anything).

Fav: You Never Give Me Your Money
Notes: The songs are good and I can bop to them fine. But it's pretty standard all throughout. I think it would make good road trip music while your friends talk all over the music; the vibes are good but you're not missing much not listening to the music. But I do like the guitar solos.
These songs make me feel like I'm in Footloose or one of those other high school movies where they all have poofy hair and leather jackets and vintage shit goes on.

Fav: Always Crashing in the Same Car
Notes: The first half of this album is a lot peppier than the remaining half. It's a lot sadder and mellow then. Its a little boring ngl later on kind of like a soundtrack. The album cover also has an orangish color which also reminds me of Dune just like some of the last songs. The last song though does have a sexy sax
I think i need a second listen through because not really sure how to feel about it. best songs include New Dawn Fades; Shadowplay
Listened to this while running. It's ok, need another shot.

Fav: Around the World/Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger
Notes: This was one of the running albums! She's a little bit yummy and good for long runs-ish. I like the lack of real lyrics for a lot of brain-intensive/brain-blanking activities.

This album was first listened to when I was in like my peak depressed era in middle school. The angst and self hatred resonated at that point in life. The rap-ish vibe and super speedy mapped to my anxiety atp
A couple songs on this stood out, but on the whole was a typical indie rock album from Wallows. I've noticed their albums tend to have one or two really good songs and the others are relatively mid
Listened to this while running and quite like it! It's kinda in between angst and anger like the bridge between depression and motivation so it's kinda a slay!

As a non-Mitski fan, I wanted to give this a shot. But the best songs were just the famous ones: Washing Machine Heart and Nobody. Otherwise doesn't really stand out much. I wished this had more unpopularized gems but it seems the internet got em all.

This gives very 'The Smiths', but it's just one guy. The key changes are a little retro. Ngl it's not all that TikTok hypes it to be, but has some mid-tier bangers. Not sure whether my opinion is because of all the hype, but it's just a teeny bit underwhelming. Maybe I need to give its lyrics a shot.

I listened to this while reading 'A Clockwork Orange' because Spotify said they vibe, and I agree. The sounds are very old and seem like they're coming from an eastern european apartment complex. Would listen again when trying to build something, seems mildly motivating without ultra hype.

I found this album through tiktok–the song 'I Have Forgiven Jesus' being the reason. From the album cover, I didn't know the singer is the lead in the Smiths. But the rest of the album is kinda mid, wouldn't really recommend on a whole (except that one song)

Brief: What I think European clubs are like
Notes: Disc 1 of the album slaps quite hard, disc 2 less so with more ambient tracks. There's a lot of rhythmic bangers which I prefer over hard EDM so big fan. I listened while running, so the beats definitely helped. I actually think the most famous song was a little dull, but the other ones were a lot better than the views on spotify indicate.

My two favourite songs were the ones I heard before I chose to pick this album. This gives very chill vibes but a bit boring and repetitive. The slightly muffled guitar playing is indie-core, but I think I've just heard too much of that.

Brief: Mildly jazzy but not snobby coffeehouse
Notes: Lowkey nothing crazy, just chill

The songs weren't bad, but nothing spectacular. I liked Cygnet Committee too. A lot of the older albums like this sound somewhat similar and a little boring in spots. But the climaxes in Space Oddity and Cygnet Committee were pretty good.

I quite like this album, but would consider it to be a little on the predictable side. It's a good, easy listen without being too basic. I also like the fact that it's in another language too. Is probably also good to run to.
Lowkey a little boring but good background music. There should be a little more uniqueness. It's one of the music slop types.
